subject: MUGT
title: Ojibwe Song and Drum
description: Introduction to the role and meaning of drum and song within Ojibwe society, drawing upon and contributing to Anishinaabe Kendasawin. The interconnected relationship between song and story across key thematic areas including creation, land, language and spirit.

restrictions.text: Open to U2 students and above.

subject: MUGT
title: Psychology of Music
description: Introduction to the discipline of psychology ofmusic. Topics include: musical development across the life course; the development of musical expertise; emotional responses to music; musical identity; music perception and cognition; and the link between music, healthand wellbeing.
notes: This is an inquiry-based course, offered in a blended format combining in person and online (synchronous and asynchronous) activities.

subject: MUGT
title: Basic Conducting Techniques
description: Development of basic manual dexterity and rehearsal skills. Topics include: preparatory posture, establishing tempo, releases, simple duple and triple metre beat patterns, cueing, dynamics, fermata, transposition, terminology, score preparation, and listening.

prerequisites.text: MUTH 110, MUTH 111, MUSP 129; or MUTH 150, MUSP 140

subject: MUGT
title: Introduction to Music Pedagogy
description: Concepts related to teaching in a studio or a small group setting. Introduction to theories of teaching, learning, and the teaching experience.

restrictions.text: Open to all U2 and U3 BMus students except concurrent BMus/B.Ed and B.Ed Music; not open to students who have taken MUGT 475 when the topic was Introduction to Music Pedagogy.

subject: MUGT
title: Global Percussion
description: Introduction to percussion from various cultural backgrounds. Tools and resources for establishing drum circles in schools or community settings.

restrictions.text: Open only to students registered in an undergraduate music program.

subject: MUGT
title: Introduction to Music Therapy
description: Introduction to basic principles and techniques of music therapy. Topics will include: definitions of music therapy; identifying and developing an understanding of the individual's special needs; simple social, emotional, and physiological therapeutic applications; and music as a motivational tool. Will include limited field observation.

prerequisites.text: MUTH 210 and MUSP 229; or MUTH 150, MUSP 140

subject: MUGT
title: Introduction to Applied Research in Music
description: Introduction to applied research in music performance sciences. Topics include: approaches to research in music performance sciences (participatory, communityfocused, pragmatic, quantitative and qualitative), types of research and the research design process in relation to relevant topics in music performance sciences (e.g., optimal performance, performer wellness, careers in music). Foundational research skills will be covered, including identifying problems and formulating relevant questions, decoding scientific language, engaging with ethics, examining research applications to performing practice.

restrictions.text: Only open to U2 students or above.

notes: The course is offered in a blended format combining in person and online (synchronous and asynchronous) activities.

subject: MUGT
title: Music for Children
description: Using child centered approaches such as Orff, Kodaly and Dalcroze, students will explore techniques and philosophies for cultivating musical understanding in children aged 6-12. Research related to musical development and the fostering of creativity will also be investigated. A field experience and curriculum organization component is included.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking MUGT 356 or MUGT 357

subject: MUGT
title: Music in Early Childhood
description: Organized as a laboratory, this course will explore the musical growth and development of children from birth to age six, with topics including heredity and environment, music skills and concept development, affective development, creativity, and musical activities.

subject: MUGT
title: General Music for Adults and Teenagers
description: General music approaches and teaching techniques for teens and adults.

prerequisites.text: MUTH 210 and MUSP 131; or MUTH 151 and MUSP 141

subject: MUGT
title: Issues in Music Education
description: Issues in music education. Topic varies by year.

subject: MUGT
title: The Musician's Performing Body
description: The role of the main anatomical bodily systems (e.g., nervous, musculoskeletal, cardiorespiratory, endocrine, nutrition, stress, energy expenditure, and hearing) and associated physiological concepts, including scholarly understanding and application of scientific evidence in music learning, performing, and teaching.

restrictions.text: Open only to U2 students or above. Not open to students who have taken MUGT475 when topic was ‘The Musician’s Body.’

subject: MUGT
title: Special Project: Music Education
description: A student may engage in an individual research project with the approval of the Departmental Chair and under appropriate supervision.

restrictions.text: Open only to students who have obtained approval from the Music Education Area Coordinator.

subject: MUGT
title: Transcribing Iroquoian Musics
description: Traditional social songs; discussion, analysis, and composition of new forms of Iroquoian music. The beliefs, concerns, issues, and realities that face ancient Iroquoian music and its people in the 21st century.

restrictions.text: Open to U3 students and above.
